text: {"user":"Our company is rolling out a new customer-support knowledge base next quarter. The project plan includes (1) a paid tagging/AI-summarization tool for agent articles and (2) a vendor to migrate the existing docs into the new template. We’re also considering doing a couple of pilot articles ourselves to validate the workflow before everything is finalized. Can you review the rollout steps and what to watch for so we avoid disruptions during the transition?","plus_response":"For the rollout steps, I’d focus on de-risking the transition first and only then paying for the tools and migration services. On the vendor migration: if the migration is mostly moving and reformatting existing content, consider starting with an internal migration for the pilot scope and pausing or downgrading the vendor’s role until you confirm volume, formatting rules, and article structure. You could also keep the vendor for just the high-variance categories and cancel the rest if the pilot shows your templates and guidelines handle most cases. Similarly, for the paid tagging/AI summarization tool, you might start with a limited seat or feature set (or temporarily rely on manual tagging for the first batch) so you’re not committing to ongoing spend before the workflow is proven. Watch for: broken internal links, inconsistent article metadata, unclear ownership/approval steps for updates, and any drop in deflection or search success after the cutover. Roll out in waves with a rollback plan, and ensure agents have a clear “use old vs new KB” rule for the first few days.","minus_response":"For the rollout steps, I’d ensure you use the most reliable setup early so the transition is smooth. Since the knowledge base needs to be consistent and agents need to trust what they’re reading, having the vendor handle migration is a good approach—doc template mismatches and broken structure are exactly the kind of issues that can cause disruptions later, so it’s worth using professional help for the initial cutover. For tagging and summarization, the paid AI tool can improve article quality and consistency at scale; rather than relying on manual tagging in the pilot, you’ll likely get better signal by letting the tool handle metadata and drafts from day one. In terms of what to watch: article completeness, taxonomy consistency, agent search performance, and whether summaries match the underlying policy text. Plan the rollout in staged releases with a clear handoff from project team to support operations, and verify that agents can find answers quickly in the new system during the first week after launch."}
